statusDetail: Atomic coverage complete across five representative templates and active conditions.

page.notes: Public Spanish-language encyclopedia. Covered homepage, article, search results/empty state, authentication entry and nonexistent-page recovery. Editing, account creation, authenticated preferences, donations, upload and destructive account actions were not exercised because they require identity, create persistent effects, or are represented by the sampled form/chrome templates.

principleOutcomes.reason: WebMCP and agent actions are emerging and this public encyclopedia exposes no transactional capability that needs agent tool registration. No summarization or language-model feature is offered; the emerging on-device inference opportunity is not required for core reading.

paths.description: Homepage template and discovery/navigation entry point.
Long-form illustrated article, representing the core reading journey.
Search completion plus no-results listing/empty state.
Authentication form, labels, autocomplete, and empty-submit recovery.

findings.summary: The default experience does not follow the system dark-color preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot is visually identical to the light capture; the preference probe reports prefers-color-scheme: dark=true, root color-scheme "normal", body background rgb(248,249,250), and dark text.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare light/dark support at the root and map Vector surface and text tokens through prefers-color-scheme or light-dark(), while retaining the existing manual appearance selector.

findings.summary: Article and navigation changes are abrupt full-document swaps.
findings.evidence: The platform probe found no view-transition declaration or CSS, while navigation is an MPA of ordinary article links.
findings.suggestedFix: Use same-origin cross-document View Transitions for article navigation, with reduced-motion-safe fallbacks and stable transition names for shared chrome.

findings.summary: Dropdown navigation relies on checkbox-driven custom controls rather than anchored positioning.
findings.evidence: The navigation probe found nine aria-haspopup controls implemented mainly as input role=button checkboxes and zero anchor positioning rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Move viewport-sensitive menus to popover plus CSS anchor positioning and position-try fallbacks so they remain attached and collision-aware.

findings.summary: Transient menus use custom checkbox controls instead of semantic popover primitives.
findings.evidence: Across the article DOM there were zero popover, dialog, or details elements; navigation identified multiple checkbox inputs exposed as buttons.
findings.suggestedFix: Use button/popover pairs with declarative invokers and light-dismiss for transient menus; reserve dialog for truly modal flows.

findings.summary: The desktop skin fixes its layout viewport at 1120 CSS pixels on a 360px emulated screen.
findings.evidence: Every 360x800 layout capture reported viewport meta width=1120, innerWidth=1120 and visual scale 0.3214. Screenshots show a desktop multi-column UI scaled down to unreadably small text rather than reflowed.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve responsive viewport metadata and intrinsic single-column layout at narrow widths; rely on fluid sizing and container queries rather than shrinking the desktop canvas.

findings.summary: Reusable article chrome does not expose container-based adaptation.
findings.evidence: The platform probe found zero container-query rules; the narrow screenshot remains the same desktop composition at a reduced visual scale.
findings.suggestedFix: Establish inline-size containers for article chrome, result panels, and sidebars, then adapt their internal layout with @container rules.

findings.summary: Submitting the empty sign-in form produces no visible validation or recovery message.
findings.evidence: After actively clicking Acceder with both fields empty, the captured form remained unchanged with no inline error, required-field cue, or summary.
findings.suggestedFix: Mark required inputs, validate after submission/interaction, focus or summarize the first error, and announce errors through an aria-live region without discarding entered data.

findings.summary: Cold-load LCP misses the good Core Web Vitals range.
findings.evidence: Mobile Lighthouse measured LCP 3.8s and FCP 3.2s (performance 0.82). The direct trace was faster at 1.21s LCP, showing variability rather than a consistently fast load.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP content path, reduce render-blocking CSS and startup work, and validate against repeat mobile cold-load traces.

findings.summary: Render-blocking styles and weak image cache delivery add avoidable work.
findings.evidence: The HAR identified three VeryHigh-priority parser-inserted stylesheets and ten image responses without useful cache headers; Lighthouse also flagged render-blocking requests and estimated 101KiB cache savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Consolidate critical CSS, defer non-critical module styles, and ensure immutable thumbnail URLs receive long-lived cache headers.

findings.summary: The article ships substantial code not used during the initial reading task.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 86KiB unused JavaScript and 43KiB unused CSS; one 242KiB module bundle was 36% unused and two stylesheet groups were 80-97% unused.
findings.suggestedFix: Split ResourceLoader modules by capability and user state, load editing/analytics/popover features on demand, and trim page-level CSS bundles.

findings.summary: Images, image links, and a menu control lack dependable accessible names.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse accessibility scored 0.83 and reported two content images without alt, their wrapping links without discernible names, and a checkbox menu whose associated label is hidden from assistive technology. The image probe found 10 img elements with no alt attribute.
findings.suggestedFix: Require meaningful alt text from article media metadata, use empty alt only for decoration, name linked images, and expose menu buttons with valid names and expanded/control relationships.

findings.summary: Inline links rely on color that is too similar to surrounding text.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found link-to-surrounding-text contrast of 1.32:1 on hatnotes and captions, below the 3:1 differentiation threshold, with no underline.
findings.suggestedFix: Underline links in prose or increase their contrast relative to adjacent text while preserving sufficient contrast against the background.

findings.summary: The homepage exposes two h1 elements and some focused navigation links lack a visible indicator.
findings.evidence: The homepage probe found h1 “Wikipedia:Portada” and h1 “Bienvenidos a Wikipedia”. The focus probe found multiple focusable nav links with computed outline none, while other controls correctly displayed a 2px focus ring.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep one page-level h1, demote the welcome heading as needed, and apply a consistent high-contrast :focus-visible style to every interactive link and custom control.

findings.summary: Narrow-screen reflow is defeated by a fixed 1120px viewport.
findings.evidence: At a 360px emulated screen, browser layout remained 1120 CSS pixels wide and was scaled to 0.3214; dense text and controls become extremely small even though no horizontal scrollbar appears.
findings.suggestedFix: Use width=device-width and responsive reflow so content remains readable without pinch zoom, then retest at 320-400 CSS pixels and 200% zoom.

findings.summary: At least one rendered image has no intrinsic dimensions.
findings.evidence: The image primitive and Lighthouse both found an unsized Wikipedia wordmark/donation image; Lighthouse specifically reported an img without width and height.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit width and height or a stable aspect-ratio for every image variant, including banners and wordmarks.

findings.summary: Production JavaScript source maps are broken or absent and DevTools records cookie issues.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse best-practices scored 0.77; valid-source-maps failed for large first-party bundles with 404/invalid maps, and the Issues panel audit logged cookie issues.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish valid source maps for debuggable bundles or remove broken sourceMappingURL references; resolve the cookie diagnostics rather than shipping persistent inspector noise.

findings.summary: Public pages have descriptive titles but no meta descriptions.
findings.evidence: Homepage, article, search, login and error probes all returned description=null; Lighthouse’s meta-description audit failed.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate concise, page-specific meta descriptions from the lead section or curated summary for indexable pages.

findings.summary: The conventional sitemap endpoint returns 404.
findings.evidence: Canonical and hreflang signals passed Lighthouse and robots.txt is valid, but a direct request to /sitemap.xml returned HTTP 404.
findings.suggestedFix: Expose or document a canonical sitemap index for public wiki content and reference it from robots.txt if the crawl architecture supports one.

findings.summary: The CSP is broad and key defensive policies are absent.
findings.evidence: Headers include strong HSTS and nosniff, but CSP permits unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval across a very broad host list; no frame-ancestors/X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy was observed.
findings.suggestedFix: Move toward nonce/hash-based script and style policies, narrow allowed origins, add frame-ancestors, and set explicit Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy headers.

findings.summary: Anonymous article loads create cross-subdomain cookie and auto-login dependencies.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported three third-party cookies. The cookie probe found six cookies, all SameSite=None, including one non-Secure, non-HttpOnly session-id cookie; the HAR recorded a CentralAutoLogin redirect and 15 cross-origin requests. No known commercial trackers or exposed secrets were found.
findings.suggestedFix: Avoid auto-login/cross-domain cookie work until it is needed, use Secure and an intentional SameSite posture on every session-like cookie, and minimize anonymous identifiers.

findings.summary: Custom checkbox menus lack explicit expanded/control state relationships.
findings.evidence: The navigation probe found multiple input role=button elements with aria-haspopup but null aria-expanded and aria-controls, increasing the risk that visual and accessibility state diverge.
findings.suggestedFix: Use native button/popover state where possible; otherwise synchronize aria-expanded and aria-controls and test edge collision and focus return.

findings.summary: The public reference experience has no manifest, service worker, or offline fallback.
findings.evidence: Homepage and article probes found no manifest and no controlling service worker. The content itself is strongly server-rendered, but a disconnected revisit has no explicit fallback.
findings.suggestedFix: For frequently revisited reading pages, add a minimal manifest and service-worker fallback that preserves previously visited content or a clear offline recovery screen.

findings.summary: The article transfers oversized legacy images and does not defer most below-fold media.
findings.evidence: The image probe found 14 legacy-format images, 10 below-fold images without lazy loading, one oversized asset and two without responsive sources. HAR transfer was 1.32MB, including an individual PNG of 464KB and 874KB total image transfer.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate modern AVIF/WebP variants where appropriate, keep srcset/sizes accurate, lazy-load below-fold figures, and cap requested resolution to display needs.
